description.7.0: This command is used to apply boundary conditions at surface faces of the model. To apply conditions to zones rather than at faces, see the zone apply command. To apply conditions at individual gridpoints, see the zone gridpoint fix command.
description.9.0: This command is used to apply boundary conditions at surface faces of the model. Process gating (verified against FLAC3D 9.7): the keyword ENUMERATION below is context-free -- the parser lists the identical 47-keyword set whether or not thermal/dynamic/creep/fluid are configured -- but EXECUTION is gated per process: thermal keywords (temperature, flux, convection) require 'model configure thermal', dynamic keywords (quiet*, acceleration*) require 'model configure dynamic', fluid keywords (pore-pressure*, head*, discharge, leakage) require a fluid configure; without the configure the engine rejects with a message naming the missing process. Applying a condition to gridpoints that already carry a conflicting apply removes the old condition (reported in the command output).

notes: '[faceapplyblock]' at the end of a keyword's syntax is not a literal token: it marks where this command's shared modifier keywords may follow (fish, fish-local, gradient, servo, table, vary, update-direction).

keywords.description: Uses head to calculate and fix pore pressures together with saturation (companion keyword to head). Requires the model configured for fluid, with fluid density and gravity defined beforehand. Verified against FLAC3D 9.7; absent from the official 9.x HTML documentation.

description.7.0: f1 is the pore pressure in the leaky layer.

keywords.name: pore-pressure-maximum
keywords.description: Seepage-type limited-pore-pressure boundary. Gridpoint pore pressure on the face is left FREE while below f (it follows the flow field, unlike a plain pore-pressure apply which pins the value from both directions) and is clamped at f whenever flow would push it higher -- the face acts as a drain at pp = f. At apply time, any pore pressure above f in the range is immediately reduced to f. Omitting f is equivalent to f = 0 (zero-pressure seepage face). Requires the model configured for fluid. State-verified against FLAC3D 9.7 (fluid-explicit diffusion tests with gp.pp() readback, contrasted against a plain pore-pressure face); absent from the official 9.x HTML documentation.

keywords.name: pore-pressure-saturation
keywords.description: Apply pore pressure and saturation together; takes a 2-component vector (pore pressure, saturation). Requires the model configured for fluid. Verified against FLAC3D 9.7; absent from the official 9.x HTML documentation.

description.7.0: Specify a multiplier that is a FISH function named s. The returned value of this FISH function is multiplied by the base value (including gradient) over all zone faces or gridpoints included in this apply condition. So a return value of 1.0 will apply the base value provided, and a return value of 0.0 will effectively remove it. This function will be called every step. If the apply condition requires a vector value, this function should also return a vector. If the apply condition requires two values, the function should return a vector and the \(z\)-component will be ignored.
description.9.0: Use the FISH function named s to compute the applied value per face/gridpoint. The function name is given as an unquoted FISH symbol; a quoted string is rejected (verified FLAC3D 9.7).

description.7.0: Specify a multiplier that is a FISH function named s, which is applied separately to each individual zone face or gridpoint affected by this apply condition. This function must take two arguments. For apply conditions that work directly on faces, the first argument is a pointer to the zone and the second argument is an integer from 1 to 6 indicating the face. For apply conditions that work on gridpoints, the first argument is a pointer to the gridpoint and the second argument is not used. This allows an apply condition to vary over time as well as space. The returned value of this FISH function is multiplied by the base value (including gradient) on the specific zone supplied. So a return value of 1.0 will apply the base value provided, and a return value of 0.0 will effectively remove it. This function will be called every step for every zone included in the apply condition. If the apply condition requires a vector value, this function should also return a vector. If the apply condition requires two values, the function should return a vector and the \(z\)-component will be ignored.
description.9.0: Use the local-namespace FISH function s to compute the applied value. The function name is given as an unquoted FISH symbol; a quoted string is rejected (verified FLAC3D 9.7).

description.7.0: Apply a gradient to the scalar-value provided. This is not available if the apply conditions requires two values or a vector value.
description.9.0: Apply a linear spatial gradient v to the base value (optionally with a reference origin).

description.7.0: Use a servo tied to the mechanical convergence ratio to control the magnitude of the applied condition. This can be used to maintain, gradually ramp up, or gradually reduce apply conditions while maintaining a quasi-static response. This controls a factor that is multiplied with the base value supplied. By default the factor will start at 0.001, and will gradually increase to 1.0 as the convergence ratio falls below 2e-3, and decrease if it rises above 1e-2. The following keywords are available to control the servo response:
description.9.0: Servo-control the applied magnitude based on the mechanical convergence ratio. Sub-keywords verified against FLAC3D 9.7: latency, lower-bound, lower-multiplier (must be > 1), maximum, minimum, ramp, ratio (one of average / convergence / global / local / maximum), reduce, upper-bound, upper-multiplier (must be < 1). Replaces the 7.0 hyphenated servo-* keywords (servo-ratio, servo-latency, ...), which FLAC3D 9.x rejects.

keywords.name: servo-latency
keywords.description: The minimum number of steps that must pass since the last servo adjustment before the next one occurs. This can keep the servo from over controlling in the initial response to a change in the factor. The default value is 1.

keywords.name: servo-lower-bound
keywords.description: Set the lower mechanical convergence ratio limit. If the current ratio falls below this limit, the factor will be multiplied by the lower-multiplier. The default limit is 2e-3.

keywords.name: servo-lower-multiplier
keywords.description: If the current ratio falls below the lower-bound limit, the factor is multiplied by this number. The default is 1.01.

keywords.name: servo-maximum
keywords.description: The maximum value the factor is allowed to become. The default is 1.0.

keywords.name: servo-minimum
keywords.description: The minimum value the factor is allowed to become. The default is 0.001.

keywords.name: servo-ramp
keywords.description: Sets the servo into ramp mode. This means that the factor is not allowed to go down, the value will only increase. This is useful to gradually increase an applied condition to it’s full value. See also the reduce keyword.

keywords.name: servo-ratio
keywords.description: Which mechanical convergence ratio is compared against lower-bound and upper-bound. By default this is the current value assigned by the zone ratio command (which is average by default. See the zone ratio command for definitions. The available keywords are:

keywords.name: servo-ratio-average
keywords.description: Use the average mechanical force ratio.

keywords.name: servo-ratio-maximum
keywords.description: Use the maximum mechanical force ratio.

keywords.name: servo-ratio-local
keywords.description: Use the local mechanical force ratio.

keywords.name: servo-reduce
keywords.description: Sets the servo into reduce mode. In this mode the starting value of the factor is 1.0, and the minimum value is set to 0.0. When the current ratio falls below lower-bound the factor is reduced by the upper-multiplier. The factor is never increased. This is useful to gradually decrease an applied condition to zero.

keywords.name: servo-upper-bound
keywords.description: Set the upper mechanical convergence ratio value. If the current ratio rises above this value, the factor will be multiplier by the upper-multiplier. The default is 1e-2.

keywords.name: servo-upper-multiplier
keywords.description: If the current ratio rises above the upper-bound, the factor is multiplied by this. The default is 0.975.

keywords.name: system
keywords.description: The local coordinate system used by the apply condition may be specified explicitly by the user. By default, this coordinate system is determined automatically. For faces it is determined by the normal direction of the face. For gridpoints it is determined by the average normal vectors of all faces connected to the gridpoint that are a part of this apply condition.

keywords.name: system-normal
keywords.description: v is the unit normal vector to the plane.

keywords.name: system-dip
keywords.description: dip [degrees], f, of the plane measured in the negative z-direction from the global xy-plane.

keywords.name: system-dip-direction
keywords.description: dip-direction [degrees], f, of the plane measured in the global xy-plane clockwise from the positive y-axis.

description.7.0: Specify a multiplier that is a table named s. By default the x-axis value is the current step number. The optional time keyword may be used to specify which processes accumulated time-total should be used to provide the x-axis value. The available keywords are:
description.9.0: Specify a value multiplier from the table named s (the x-value of the table is time by default). The table name must be given as a quoted string (e.g. table 'name'); an unquoted name is rejected. Replaces the 7.0 table-creep / table-dynamic / table-fluid / table-mechanical / table-step / table-thermal variants, which FLAC3D 9.x no longer accepts. Verified against FLAC3D 9.7.

description.7.0: Apply a linear variation to the scalar-value provided. This is not available if the apply conditions requires two values or a vector value.
description.9.0: Apply a linear variation v to the base value across the face.

keywords.name: update-direction
keywords.description: If on, the direction of the applied vector quantity is updated each step to follow the current face normal (for large-strain analyses). Verified FLAC3D 9.7: accepted after gridpoint-based vector conditions (velocity, velocity-normal, acceleration, ...); rejected after face-based stress conditions (stress-normal, stress-xx, ...).

keywords.name: cutoff
keywords.description: Follows head or pore-pressure. Pore-pressure values are not allowed to fall below this value. If no value is given 0.0 is assumed. The default is no limit.

keywords.name: datum
keywords.description: Follows head. The datum used as the origin of the head height; the applied pore pressure is density * gravity * (head - height above the datum). The default value is the origin.

keywords.name: free-field
keywords.description: Free-field boundary condition (dynamic analysis). Verified live against FLAC3D 7.0 (first-token enumeration, 2026-08-13).

description.7.0: Apply a full stress tensor on faces. Verified live against FLAC3D 7.0 (first-token enumeration, 2026-08-13).
description.9.0: Apply the full stress tensor (six components) as a face traction condition.

keywords.name: westergaard
keywords.description: Westergaard hydrodynamic pressure condition (moved to the dedicated zone face westergaard command in 9.x). Verified live against FLAC3D 7.0 (first-token enumeration, 2026-08-13).

keywords.name: reaction-tangential
keywords.description: Reaction force, tangential component. (2D only.)

keywords.name: stress-shear
keywords.description: Apply shear traction. (2D only.)

keywords.name: velocity-tangential
keywords.description: Velocity in the tangential direction. (2D only.)
